thread:
maria: quick async standup — kernel/batching/KV perf.

maria: yesterday: landed the prefetch tweak that reduces cold p95 by ~12% on short sequences. pushed canary to stage.

jon: nice! saw reduced p95 on stage traces. noticed one spike around 2.3s on a few shard IDs. digging.

priya: thanks — FYI the canary has the new slot allocator enabled, may interact with eviction. adding logs to correlate.

maria: blocker: one of the stress benches on stage OOM'd after long-run, need help reproducing locally.

ash: i can repro with the perf harness. sharing command: `./bench --profile=kv-warmup --shards=8 --duration=30m`

ash: initial hypothesis: kv prefault + aggressive microbatching causes memory spike when many long contexts line up.

jon: good call. i'll add a histogram for KV cache size and microbatch depth to the canary. should help isolate.

priya: question: do we want to roll back slot allocator if OOMs persist, or throttle microbatching instead?

maria: prefer throttle microbatching first — less user-visible. plan: add a soft cap on microbatch depth at 48 for canary and rerun.

ops-bot: deploy noted — canary config updated by maria (change: microbatch.max_depth=48). :white_check_mark:

jon: running a full 2h bench now, will post results.

priya: quick code-review ping @jon on PR #4123 (slot allocator logging) — 1 small nits.

jon: on it, will address and merge if green.

maria: today: monitor canary + verify no regression in latency/cost. if stable, promote to smoke-prod.

ash: i'll follow up with a minimal repro script and memory traces.

maria: thanks all. if anyone hits the OOM, drop logs here and tag me. otherwise i'll update later with canary outcome. :thumbsup:

jon: noted. ttyl.
